sentences.en: I'm Lulu Garcia Navarro and today I'm interviewing Ina Garten.
sentences.zh: 我是露露·加西亚-纳瓦罗，今天我将采访伊娜·加滕。

sentences.en: Garten's best known for her cookbooks and her show Barefoot Contessa,
sentences.zh: 加滕最出名的是她的食谱和节目《赤脚主妇》,

sentences.en: which premiered on the Food Network almost 24 years ago.
sentences.zh: 该节目近24年前在食品频道首播。

sentences.en: I'm always looking for new ways to cook chicken, but nothing says summer more than cooking chicken on a grill.
sentences.zh: 我总是在寻找烹饪鸡肉的新方法，但没有什么比在烤架上烤鸡更能代表夏天了。

sentences.en: That show taught people how to cook.
sentences.zh: 那个节目教人们如何做饭。

sentences.en: A quarter of a cup of olive oil, a cup of onion.
sentences.zh: 四分之一杯橄榄油，一杯洋葱。

sentences.en: How to entertain.
sentences.zh: 如何待客。

sentences.en: So I'm going to have cocktails and hors d'oeuvres on the porch.
sentences.zh: 所以我打算在门廊上准备鸡尾酒和开胃菜。

sentences.en: I'm going to have dinner on the dining room table.
sentences.zh: 我打算在餐厅的桌上享用晚餐。

sentences.en: It's going to be casual.
sentences.zh: 这将是一场轻松的聚会。

sentences.en: And how to be unfussy about it.
sentences.zh: 以及如何对此不拘小节。

sentences.en: You can use ingredients from the store like a pound cake or vanilla ice cream that are just as good as homemade.
sentences.zh: 你可以使用店里的食材，比如磅蛋糕或香草冰淇淋，它们和自制的一样好。

sentences.en: Garten's laid back style and plucky personality made her both a household name and a cult figure.
sentences.zh: 加滕轻松的风格和勇敢的个性使她既家喻户晓，又具有邪典偶像般的地位。

sentences.en: Delicious.
sentences.zh: 太美味了。

sentences.en: Lovingly parodied and memed on social media.
sentences.zh: 在社交媒体上被亲切地恶搞和做成表情包。

sentences.en: Tonight I'm making a wonderful dinner and it starts with brownie pudding.
sentences.zh: 今晚我要做一顿美妙的晚餐，从布朗尼布丁开始。

sentences.en: And now at 78, she's doing something new.
sentences.zh: 如今78岁的她正在做一些新鲜事。

sentences.en: Launching a video podcast called Happy Hour with Ina.
sentences.zh: 推出一个名为《与伊娜的欢乐时光》的视频播客。

sentences.en: And her 14th cookbook, Simply Ina, is coming out this fall.
sentences.zh: 她的第14本食谱《简单伊娜》将于今年秋天问世。

sentences.en: Here's my conversation with Ina Gartner.
sentences.zh: 以下是我与伊娜·加滕的对话。

sentences.en: I am thrilled to have you here.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴能邀请到你。

sentences.en: I have watched you for such a long time.
sentences.zh: 我看你的节目已经很久了。

sentences.en: I have cooked your recipes.
sentences.zh: 我一直照着你的食谱做菜。

sentences.en: And so it is a great pleasure to welcome you to the interview, Ina.
sentences.zh: 所以非常高兴能欢迎你来接受采访，伊娜。

sentences.en: Thank you, Lulu.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，露露。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I love what you do too.
sentences.zh: 我也很喜欢你的节目。

sentences.en: So I'm so thrilled to be here.
sentences.zh: 所以我很高兴能来到这里。

sentences.en: Really honored.
sentences.zh: 真的很荣幸。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I've been doing the math on your life.
sentences.zh: 我算了一下你的人生经历。

sentences.en: Uh-oh.
sentences.zh: 噢哦。

sentences.en: You're now 78 years old.
sentences.zh: 你现在78岁了。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And you are just about to start this whole new chapter.
sentences.zh: 而你正准备开启一个全新的篇章。

sentences.en: You are launching a podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 你要推出一个播客。

sentences.en: I am.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you started your Celebrated Food Network TV show when you were in your mid-50s.
sentences.zh: 你在50多岁时推出了你那个著名的食品频道电视节目。

sentences.en: And you wrote your first cookbook when you were in your early 50s.
sentences.zh: 你在50岁出头时写了你的第一本食谱。

sentences.en: And I find this very inspirational as a woman also in my 50s.
sentences.zh: 作为一个也处在50多岁的女性，我觉得这非常鼓舞人心。

sentences.en: What have you learned about taking on challenges in later life?
sentences.zh: 对于在晚年迎接挑战，你有什么心得？

sentences.en: I think that when I look back and I think about the things that I've done, like writing cookbooks, and I love working scared because it keeps me up at night.
sentences.zh: 我想，当我回首过去，想起我做过的事情，比如写食谱，我喜欢带着恐惧感工作，因为这让我夜不能寐。

sentences.en: So I love, you know, I love this expression, getting out over your skis.
sentences.zh: 我真的很喜欢“超越自身能力极限”这种说法。

sentences.en: Well, you have no choice.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你别无选择。

sentences.en: You've invested your money.
sentences.zh: 你已经投入了资金。

sentences.en: You've, you know, sort of made a stake in what you've decided to do, whether it's books or TV.
sentences.zh: 你已经在你决定要做的事情上押注了，无论是书还是电视。

sentences.en: And very often I've said no to things for years until I figured out how can I do this differently?
sentences.zh: 很多时候，我多年来一直在拒绝各种事情，直到我想清楚：我该如何以不同的方式来做？

sentences.en: Like I don't like doing it the way everybody else does it.
sentences.zh: 就像我不喜欢用别人的方式去做。

sentences.en: I like doing, taking something like books and saying, most cookbooks are in, when I started in 1999, most cookbooks had like 250 recipes.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢把像书这样的东西拿来研究，心想，大多数食谱书在1999年我刚开始时，里面大约有250道菜谱。

sentences.en: I mean, who needs 250 recipes?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，谁需要250道食谱？

sentences.en: I need 75 really good recipes that I can make over and over again.
sentences.zh: 我只需要75道真正好吃的食谱，我可以一遍又一遍地做。

sentences.en: And so when I decided to write cookbooks, I thought, okay, I'm going to write this book.
sentences.zh: 所以当我决定写食谱时，我想，好吧，我要写这本书。

sentences.en: I'm not even sure my publisher was convinced that it was going to work.
sentences.zh: 我甚至不确定我的出版商是否相信这会成功。

sentences.en: But it worked out okay.
sentences.zh: 但结果还不错。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think one of the things, though, that happens when people get older in particular is that you get more afraid, you know.
sentences.zh: 是的，不过我发现人变老时发生的一件事，就是你会变得更害怕，你知道的。

sentences.en: Get more afraid?
sentences.zh: 变得更害怕？

sentences.en: Oh, that's interesting.
sentences.zh: 哦，这真有意思。

sentences.en: I thought you were going to say get more confident.
sentences.zh: 我还以为你会说变得更自信。

sentences.en: No, I don't.
sentences.zh: 不，我没有。

sentences.en: Isn't that interesting?
sentences.zh: 这难道不有趣吗？

sentences.en: I actually don't think people get more.
sentences.zh: 我其实不觉得人们会变得更……

sentences.en: You have more to lose?
sentences.zh: 你有了更多要失去的东西？

sentences.en: Well, you have more to lose.
sentences.zh: 嗯，你确实有更多要失去的。

sentences.en: You get more set in your ways, you know.
sentences.zh: 你会变得更墨守成规，你知道的。

sentences.en: I'm just the opposite, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Yeah, I know, and I think that's such a great lesson, but I think it's unusual.
sentences.zh: 对，我知道，我觉得这是个很好的经验，但我认为这很不寻常。

sentences.en: I think I have a very low threshold of boredom.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我对无聊的忍耐度很低。

sentences.en: If I know how to do something, I don't want to do it again.
sentences.zh: 如果我知道怎么做一件事，我就不想再做一遍了。

sentences.en: I love using what I've learned and figuring out the next step.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢运用我所学到的知识并琢磨下一步。

sentences.en: It's really clear for me.
sentences.zh: 这对我来说非常清晰。

sentences.en: I ask myself one question.
sentences.zh: 我只问自己一个问题。

sentences.en: Is it going to be fun?
sentences.zh: 这会好玩吗？

sentences.en: And if it's fun, then I really want to do it.
sentences.zh: 如果好玩，那我真的很想去做。

sentences.en: I just have to figure out how to make sure it's fun.
sentences.zh: 我只需要想办法确保它充满乐趣。

sentences.en: I mean, it's working with people that I love working with.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这得和那些我喜欢合作的人一起工作。

sentences.en: It's working with creative people.
sentences.zh: 和有创意的人一起工作。

sentences.en: I mean, in the cookbook, I have food stylists doing the photographs and photographer.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在食谱里，我有负责拍照的美食造型师和摄影师。

sentences.en: There are people I look forward to working together, where we create something that's better than any one of us alone, and I'm responsible for the team.
sentences.zh: 这些是我期待合作的人，我们共同创造出超越我们任何单个人水平的东西，而我对这个团队负责。

sentences.en: I love that feeling.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那种感觉。

sentences.en: It's kind of like a great ballet where everybody's working together.
sentences.zh: 有点像一场伟大的芭蕾舞，每个人都在齐心协力。

sentences.en: So I like that feeling of building something with people.
sentences.zh: 所以我喜欢这种和大家一起构建某些东西的感觉。

sentences.en: Well, let's talk about the two new projects that you have coming out.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们来聊聊你即将推出的两个新项目。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: A podcast and a new cookbook.
sentences.zh: 一个播客和一本新食谱。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Um, let's start with the cookbook.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们从食谱开始吧。

sentences.en: It's the first one in four years.
sentences.zh: 这是四年来的第一本。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Uh, it's called Simply Ina.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它叫《简单伊娜》。

sentences.en: The recipes all look easy and delicious, which are your signature.
sentences.zh: 这些食谱看起来都简单又美味，这是你的标志性风格。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Um, have you ever been tempted to make something off-brand, complicated Ina, fussy Ina, you know, pretentious Ina?
sentences.zh: 嗯，你有没有想过做一些不符合你风格的东西，比如复杂的伊娜、繁琐的伊娜，你知道的，装腔作势的伊娜？

sentences.en: Um, let's make cassoulet, right?
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们来做个卡苏莱砂锅吧，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, let's make cassoulet.
sentences.zh: 对，我们来做卡苏莱。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Um, no.
sentences.zh: 嗯，不。

sentences.en: I actually am not that good at cook.
sentences.zh: 其实我不太擅长烹饪。

sentences.en: I think of myself more as a taster.
sentences.zh: 我更认为自己是一个品尝者。

sentences.en: I know what I'm looking for in flavor and texture, but, um, I don't like spending hours in the kitchen cooking.
sentences.zh: 我知道我在寻找什么样的风味和口感，但是，嗯，我不想花几个小时在厨房里做饭。

sentences.en: I really don't.
sentences.zh: 我真的不想。

sentences.en: When I wrote my first book, which was the Barefoot Contessa cookbook, I decided I wanted to have several things.
sentences.zh: 当我写第一本书《赤脚主妇食谱》时，我决定要包含几件事。

sentences.en: I wanted to have, um, gorgeous photographs so that when you looked at it, you thought, oh, that looks delicious, and then you looked at the recipe and you thought, I could actually
sentences.zh: 我希望有，嗯，华丽的照片，这样当你看到它时，你会想，哦，看起来真美味，然后你看到食谱，心想，我其实

sentences.en: make that recipe, and then you looked at the ingredients and thought, oh, I can get all those ingredients in my local grocery store.
sentences.zh: 能做出那道菜，接着你看了看配料，心想，哦，我可以在当地的杂货店买齐所有这些配料。

sentences.en: That was a guiding principle of the first book, and it's still the guiding principle.
sentences.zh: 那是第一本书的指导原则，现在依然是指导原则。

sentences.en: And there may be a few things like truffle butter that you, you know, can order online and keep in the freezer, but very, very few things like that.
sentences.zh: 可能有些像松露黄油这样的小东西，你可以，你知道的，在网上订购并放在冰箱里，但极少有这样的东西。

sentences.en: Most things you can buy locally, and because this is about keeping things simple, it's even, the recipes are even easier.
sentences.zh: 大多数东西你都可以在本地买到，而且因为这旨在保持简单，所以这些食谱甚至更加简单了。

sentences.en: Do you like eating complicated food?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢吃复杂的食物吗？

sentences.en: Like, when you go to a restaurant, do you order complicated food?
sentences.zh: 比如，当你去餐馆时，你会点复杂的食物吗？

sentences.en: Hate it.
sentences.zh: 讨厌。

sentences.en: Hate it.
sentences.zh: 讨厌。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Oh, wow.
sentences.zh: 噢，哇。

sentences.en: I'm the first one who's going to order a roast chicken in a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 我是那种在餐馆里头一个点烤鸡的人。

sentences.en: No, I really don't like complicated food, and I don't like tasting menus.
sentences.zh: 不，我真的不喜欢复杂的食物，我也不喜欢品尝菜单。

sentences.en: They give me a headache.
sentences.zh: 它们让我头疼。

sentences.en: Neither do I.
sentences.zh: 我也不喜欢。

sentences.en: All those flavors, just like, oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 所有那些味道，简直就是，哦，天哪。

sentences.en: And I don't like when somebody puts something down on, you know, in front of me that I have no idea what it is.
sentences.zh: 而且我不喜欢有人把某种我完全不知道是什么的东西端到我面前。

sentences.en: I just, I'm not an adventurous eater at all, and I think my recipes reflect that.
sentences.zh: 我只是，我一点也不是个喜欢冒险的食客，我觉得我的食谱反映了这一点。

sentences.en: I like, you know, raspberry cheesecake.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢，你知道的，树莓芝士蛋糕。

sentences.en: You know, like, you know exactly what it's going to taste like.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，就像，你完全知道它会是什么味道。

sentences.en: Let's talk about your podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我们来聊聊你的播客。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: You'll be making cocktails and mocktails with a gueSt.
sentences.zh: 你将和嘉宾一起制作含酒精和不含酒精的鸡尾酒。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: Well, I mean, I'm going to serve a cocktail and mocktail to each person.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我的意思是，我要为每个人端上一杯鸡尾酒和无醇鸡尾酒。

sentences.en: Oh, you're not going to make it with them.
sentences.zh: 哦，你不是和他们一起做。

sentences.en: No, we're not going to make it.
sentences.zh: 不，我们不一起做。

sentences.en: Yeah, exactly.
sentences.zh: 对，没错。

sentences.en: Okay, all right.
sentences.zh: 好吧，行。

sentences.en: So, day drinking with Ina.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是和伊娜一起白天喝酒吗？

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 不，不是。

sentences.en: It's not day drinking with Ina.
sentences.zh: 这不是和伊娜一起白天喝酒。

sentences.en: That sounds great.
sentences.zh: 听起来很棒。

sentences.en: No, people are invited at five o'clock.
sentences.zh: 不，大家是五点钟来。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So, it's cocktail hour.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是鸡尾酒时间。

sentences.en: It's cocktail hour.
sentences.zh: 这是鸡尾酒时间。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: But it's really about the conversation.
sentences.zh: 但重点其实在于交流。

sentences.en: What makes a good conversation for you?
sentences.zh: 对你来说，怎样的交流才算好呢？

sentences.en: I think what I'm always looking for is where I connect with the gueSt.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我一直在寻找的是能与嘉宾产生共鸣的地方。

sentences.en: So, for example, with Alison Roman, she writes cookbooks.
sentences.zh: 比如艾莉森·罗曼，她写食谱。

sentences.en: She has a specialty food store in upstate New York.
sentences.zh: 她在纽约州北部开了一家特色食品店。

sentences.en: We have a lot of common experiences.
sentences.zh: 我们有很多相似的经历。

sentences.en: And so, it's really fun to talk about how she sees building a business, how she sees writing recipes.
sentences.zh: 所以，聊聊她如何看待建立商业版图、如何看待创作食谱，真的非常有趣。

sentences.en: I think that's what I'm always looking for.
sentences.zh: 我想这就是我一直在找的东西。

sentences.en: And it's interesting, no matter what the guest does, whether it's a movie director or a writer like Ann Patchett, we always can find a common thread.
sentences.zh: 很有意思的是，无论嘉宾是做什么的，不管是电影导演还是像安·帕切特这样的作家，我们总能找到共同点。

sentences.en: You know, I think having a good conversation also means having a little bit of tension at some point.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我认为进行一场好的对话，也意味着在某个时刻带有一点点紧张感。

sentences.en: But I think that's probably not your philosophy.
sentences.zh: 但我想这大概不是你的哲学。

sentences.en: Am I right?
sentences.zh: 我说的对吗？

sentences.en: I hadn't thought about it.
sentences.zh: 我之前没想过这个问题。

sentences.en: But now I'm going to.
sentences.zh: 不过现在我要开始想了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Like, what's tension in a conversation where you disagree about something?
sentences.zh: 比如说，在对某事有分歧的对话中，什么是紧张感？

sentences.en: You know, there are a lot of celebrity podcasts now where famous people interview other famous people.
sentences.zh: 你知道，现在有很多名人播客，就是名人采访其他名人。

sentences.en: And they're very friendly and they're very fun.
sentences.zh: 他们非常友好，也很有趣。

sentences.en: But I think they often steer clear of difficult questions or touchy questions in part because the interviewer and the interviewee are either friends or they're in the same social circles or you're going to see them again at some point.
sentences.zh: 但我认为他们往往会避开困难或棘手的问题，部分原因在于采访者和被采访者要么是朋友，要么身处同一个社交圈，或者你以后还会遇到他们。

sentences.en: And sometimes the conversations don't go very deep.
sentences.zh: 有时候对话不会很深入。

sentences.en: They kind of skirt the surface.
sentences.zh: 只是流于表面。

sentences.en: And I was just wondering, have you thought about how you navigate that?
sentences.zh: 我只是在想，你有没有考虑过如何应对这种情况？

sentences.en: I actually think it should be fun.
sentences.zh: 我其实觉得这应该很有趣。

sentences.en: I think the person should have an interesting point of view.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个人应该有有趣的观点。

sentences.en: But I'm really conscious that I want every conversation to have things that the listener can take away.
sentences.zh: 但我真的很在意，我希望每一次对话都能让听众有所收获。

sentences.en: So, it's not just you and I are talking.
sentences.zh: 所以，不仅仅是你和我在这里聊天。

sentences.en: It's that we're sharing our experience about how we do something.
sentences.zh: 而是我们在分享关于如何做好某件事的经验。

sentences.en: Allison and I talked about a book that I had read called Why We Buy, like how people shop.
sentences.zh: 我和艾莉森聊过一本书，我读过的那本叫《我们为什么买买买》，讲人们是怎么购物的。

sentences.en: And I'm sure somebody listening is going to go out and buy that book and it's going to change how they retail whatever it is they're selling.
sentences.zh: 我确信听节目的某个人会去买那本书，并且它会改变他们所售商品的零售方式。

sentences.en: So, my goal is not just to have a really interesting conversation but to connect with the audience.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的目标不仅是进行一场非常有趣的对话，还要与听众产生连接。

sentences.en: And that's the way I write cookbooks and it's the way I do the TV show.
sentences.zh: 我写食谱是这样，做电视节目也是这样。

sentences.en: It's what's the user experience?
sentences.zh: 重点是用户体验是什么？

sentences.en: Is it enjoyable to listen to and do you learn something from it?
sentences.zh: 听起来愉快吗，你能从中学到东西吗？

sentences.en: And the other thing is I think it's really important to ask questions you don't know the answer to and let go of control of the conversation.
sentences.zh: 另一件事是，我认为提出你不知道答案的问题，并放开对谈话的控制，这真的很重要。

sentences.en: Why did you want to do this?
sentences.zh: 你为什么想做这个？

sentences.en: Why did you want to have a podcast, which is nowadays a TV show because it's going to be filmed, obviously.
sentences.zh: 你为什么想做一档播客——现在它是一档电视节目了，因为显然要被拍成视频。

sentences.en: Because I think it really goes back to my childhood where I couldn't connect with my parents.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得这真的可以追溯到我的童年，那时我无法与父母建立情感连接。

sentences.en: And I crave that connection with people.
sentences.zh: 我渴望与人建立那种连接。

sentences.en: And that's why my friends are very important.
sentences.zh: 这就是为什么我的朋友对我很重要。

sentences.en: And I find this so interesting, the stories that people have told me on Be My Guest, like Emily Blunt talking about having a stutter, which was debilitating when she was a child.
sentences.zh: 我觉得在《做客》节目中大家跟我讲的故事非常有意思，比如艾米莉·布朗特谈到自己曾有口吃，这在她小时候是个极大的困扰。

sentences.en: And so I find people's stories really inspiring.
sentences.zh: 因此，我觉得人们的故事非常鼓舞人心。

sentences.en: And it's the difficult things in their lives that have led to the things that have changed, like Marcus Samuelsson.
sentences.zh: 正是他们生活中的艰难险阻，带来了改变命运的事物，比如马库斯·萨穆埃尔松。

sentences.en: Do you know the story of Marcus Samuelsson?
sentences.zh: 你知道马库斯·萨穆埃尔松的故事吗？

sentences.en: When he was three years old, he, his mother, and his five-year-old sister got tuberculosis.
sentences.zh: 在他三岁的时候，他和母亲以及五岁的姐姐都得了结核病。

sentences.en: And their mother walked them from the village in Ethiopia where they lived to a hospital to get treatment.
sentences.zh: 他们的母亲带着他们从埃塞俄比亚的老家步行到医院接受治疗。

sentences.en: And I don't know how long.
sentences.zh: 我不知道走了多久。

sentences.en: It was like 20 miles without shoes.
sentences.zh: 大概有20英里，而且没穿鞋。

sentences.en: Walked to this treatment center.
sentences.zh: 步行去这个治疗中心。

sentences.en: And the mother died and left two children.
sentences.zh: 母亲去世了，留下了两个孩子。

sentences.en: And a nurse knew that there was somebody in Sweden that was interested in adopting a young boy.
sentences.zh: 有个护士知道瑞典有人对收养一个小男孩感兴趣。

sentences.en: And she called and said, I have a young boy, but he has a sister, and I won't break them up.
sentences.zh: 她打电话说，我有一个小男孩，但他还有一个姐姐，我不会把他们分开。

sentences.en: And the Swedish family said, send them both.
sentences.zh: 瑞典的那个家庭说，把他们两个都送来吧。

sentences.en: So Marcus Samuelsson ended up, from the worst thing that could possibly happen to you, he lost his mother when he was three with a Swedish family.
sentences.zh: 于是马库斯·萨穆埃尔松经历了可能降临在你身上的最糟糕的事情——他在三岁时失去了母亲，但随后被一个瑞典家庭收养。

sentences.en: And the grandmother said, come, come cook with me.
sentences.zh: 祖母说，来，来跟我一起做饭。

sentences.en: How did this happen?
sentences.zh: 这怎么发生的呢？

sentences.en: He's a brilliant cook.
sentences.zh: 他是个杰出的厨师。

sentences.en: And he's got fabulous restaurants.
sentences.zh: 他拥有无与伦比的餐厅。

sentences.en: Never would have happened if the worst thing in his life hadn't happened at that moment.
sentences.zh: 如果他生命中最糟糕的事情当时没有发生，这一切永远都不会发生。

sentences.en: What is that for you?
sentences.zh: 对你来说，那是什么？

sentences.en: What is that origin story for you?
sentences.zh: 对你来说，那个最初的起点是什么？

sentences.en: Well, I think that I had a very tough childhood, and it was lonely, and it was—
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得我的童年非常艰难，而且很孤独，那是——

sentences.en: You had a mother who was very—
sentences.zh: 你的母亲非常——

sentences.en: Disconnected.
sentences.zh: 疏离。

sentences.en: Disconnected.
sentences.zh: 疏离。

sentences.en: And my father was always mad at me.
sentences.zh: 而且我父亲总是对我很生气。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: I don't know why.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么。

sentences.en: But—because he tried to control me.
sentences.zh: 但是——因为他试图控制我。

sentences.en: So, I mean, what goes in early goes in deep, and I'm always trying to recreate what I craved when I was a kid.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，早年的经历影响深远，我总是在试图重现我小时候所渴望的东西。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think either people repeat their parents' mistakes.
sentences.zh: 对，我觉得人们要么会重复父母的错误。

sentences.en: Well, that's intentionality.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是刻意为之。

sentences.en: Yeah, or they really try to move away from it.
sentences.zh: 是的，要么就是极力想要摆脱它。

sentences.en: I had a lot of help figuring out what happened, because I don't think I understood it until I was probably 40.
sentences.zh: 我得到了很多帮助才弄清楚这一切是怎么回事，因为我觉得直到我大概40岁时才真正理解。

sentences.en: And then, once you understand it, and you say, oh, that wasn't everybody's childhood.
sentences.zh: 然后，一旦你明白了，并且你会说，哦，原来不是每个人的童年都那样。

sentences.en: When you're a kid, you think everybody lives like that.
sentences.zh: 当你还是个孩子的时候，你以为所有人都那样生活。

sentences.en: And then you realize, no, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 然后你意识到，不，并不是。

sentences.en: And you make a decision to do it differently.
sentences.zh: 于是你决定做出改变。

sentences.en: Your history isn't necessarily your life.
sentences.zh: 你的过往并不注定就是你的人生。

sentences.en: You have to break free of it at some point.
sentences.zh: 你必须在某个时刻挣脱出来。

sentences.en: You have to figure it out, and then decide how you want to live.
sentences.zh: 你必须弄清楚情况，然后决定你想怎么生活。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Your story can be seen as a series of beginnings or actually a series of endings.
sentences.zh: 你的故事可以被看作是一系列的新开始，或者实际上是一系列的结束。

sentences.en: As I was sort of looking at things, you stopped catering at a certain point, and catering had helped sort of propel you into the food world when you had your specialty store.
sentences.zh: 当我回顾这些事情时，你曾在某个时间点停止了承办餐饮，而在你拥有特色食品店时，承办餐饮曾帮助你进入了餐饮世界。

sentences.en: It was allowing you to be in people's houses, and, you know, it was a lot of your business initially, and you just decided it wasn't working out.
sentences.zh: 它让你能够走进人们的家中，而且，你知道，这最初占了你业务很大一部分，但你偏偏决定不做了。

sentences.en: Because I would run Barefoot Contessa during the day, and then at 4 or 5 o'clock, we would do like 10 parties at night, and I'd get home at 1 o'clock in the morning exhausted.
sentences.zh: 因为我白天要经营“赤脚女佣”，然后到下午4点或5点，我们晚上要做好几场派对，我回到家时已经是凌晨1点，精疲力竭。

sentences.en: And on Sunday, my only day off was, you know, it was basically the afternoon I had off.
sentences.zh: 而周日我唯一的一天假，基本上只有下午能休息。

sentences.en: I couldn't even talk.
sentences.zh: 我都说不出话来。

sentences.en: I was so exhausted.
sentences.zh: 我太累了。

sentences.en: And I thought, okay, this is not working.
sentences.zh: 我想，好吧，这样行不通。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Because it really – I couldn't work and have a personal life at the same time.
sentences.zh: 因为确实——我无法一边工作一边拥有个人生活。

sentences.en: And then you sold your iconic store for similar reasons.
sentences.zh: 然后你出于类似的原因卖掉了你那标志性的店铺。

sentences.en: I think I sold the store because I knew how to do it.
sentences.zh: 我想我卖掉那家店是因为我已经知道怎么做了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: And it was no longer a challenge.
sentences.zh: 它不再是一个挑战了。

sentences.en: And I think if you're not bringing new energy and new ideas to a business, it's time to pass it off to somebody else who will.
sentences.zh: 我认为，如果你没有为一项业务带来新的能量和新的想法，是时候把它转交给其他人了。

sentences.en: And then you stopped selling prepared foods at a certain point.
sentences.zh: 后来你在某个时间点也停止销售熟食了。

sentences.en: You know, some people expand their business.
sentences.zh: 你知道，有些人会扩大他们的业务。

sentences.en: They just keep adding and adding.
sentences.zh: 他们只是不断地做加法。

sentences.en: And you seem to replace.
sentences.zh: 而你似乎是在用新事物替代旧事物。

sentences.en: And I thought that that was very interesting.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这非常有趣。

sentences.en: It is interesting.
sentences.zh: 确实很有趣。

sentences.en: I don't expand it.
sentences.zh: 我不是在扩张。

sentences.en: I do it sequentially.
sentences.zh: 我是按顺序一件一件地做。

sentences.en: You're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 你完全说得对。

sentences.en: I hadn't thought about it that way.
sentences.zh: 我以前没这么想过。

sentences.en: I think that when I know how to do something, I don't want to do it anymore.
sentences.zh: 我觉得当我懂得了如何做一件事时，我就不想再做了。

sentences.en: It's really that simple.
sentences.zh: 就是这么简单。

sentences.en: And, I mean, sometimes I've taken – you know, one time I took a year off to try and figure out what to do next.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，有时候我经历过——你知道，有一次我休息了一整年，试图弄清楚接下来该做什么。

sentences.en: And I remember in the middle of that thing, this is the worst year I've ever had because I have nothing to do, which is not my favorite thing.
sentences.zh: 我记得在那段日子的中间，这是我度过的最糟糕的一年，因为我无所事事，这不是我喜欢的生活状态。

sentences.en: But I never would have started writing cookbooks if I hadn't done it.
sentences.zh: 但如果不是那样，我永远也不会开始写食谱。

sentences.en: I did it just to have something to do.
sentences.zh: 我做这件事只是为了找点事干。

sentences.en: And it turned out to be so much more interesting than I expected.
sentences.zh: 结果它比我预期的要有趣得多。

sentences.en: So I think I kind of like the journey, you know, like just finding out where my place is and what works.
sentences.zh: 所以我想我有点喜欢这种探索的过程，你知道的，就是去发现我的位置在哪里，什么方法才管用。

sentences.en: And I always see it as like tapping on a wall and just tap, tap, tap until I hear like a hollow sound and I'm like, okay, that's where I'm going to go.
sentences.zh: 我总是把这看作是在敲墙，不停地敲、敲、敲，直到听到空洞的声音，然后我会想，好吧，我要往那个方向走。

sentences.en: And it's not what I'm going to finish with.
sentences.zh: 这并不是我最终要完成的目标。

sentences.en: It's what I'm going to start and I'm going to see where this leads.
sentences.zh: 这是我的起点，我要看看这会把我带向何方。

sentences.en: And maybe because I like to have control over what I'm doing.
sentences.zh: 也许是因为我喜欢掌控自己正在做的事情。

sentences.en: I don't like expanding it with more and more people and bigger.
sentences.zh: 我不喜欢通过招募越来越多的人和把规模做大来扩张。

sentences.en: I like doing things sequentially.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢按部就班地做事。

sentences.en: I hadn't thought about it that way, but you're absolutely right.
sentences.zh: 我以前没从这个角度想过，但你完全说得对。

sentences.en: You've always spoken about learning to trust your instincts.
sentences.zh: 你总是谈到要学会相信自己的直觉。

sentences.en: And I think that's one of the hardest things for women in particular, especially to do.
sentences.zh: 我认为这尤其是女性最难做到的一点。

sentences.en: Our inner voice is sometimes our harshest critic.
sentences.zh: 我们内心的声音有时是我们最严厉的批评者。

sentences.en: How did you learn to trust yourself?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么学会相信自己的？

sentences.en: I think my husband taught me because I think as a child I was always taught that whatever I wanted to do was a bad idea.
sentences.zh: 我觉得是我的丈夫教会了我，因为我觉得小时候我总被教导说我想做的事都是个坏主意。

sentences.en: And when I married Jeffrey, I think he always said he always supported whatever I wanted to do and encouraged it and didn't question it.
sentences.zh: 当我嫁给杰弗里之后，我觉得他总是支持我想做的任何事，鼓励我，从不质疑。

sentences.en: And I think I really learned how to be in the world that way.
sentences.zh: 我想我真的是以那种方式学会了如何在世界上自处。

sentences.en: Because you met him when you were 16.
sentences.zh: 因为你16岁就认识他了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是啊。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Very, very young.
sentences.zh: 非常非常年轻。

sentences.en: He saw you when you went to go visit your brother.
sentences.zh: 你去看望哥哥的时候他注意到了你。

sentences.en: Brother in Dartmouth, yeah.
sentences.zh: 在达特茅斯找我哥哥时，对。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Just the luckiest thing that could ever happen to anybody.
sentences.zh: 这是任何人身上能发生的最幸运的事情了。

sentences.en: I had gone from such a negative childhood to such a positive life.
sentences.zh: 我从一个如此消极的童年，走进了如此积极的人生。

sentences.en: I mean, where everything I do he thinks is brilliant and encouraged me to do more of it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我做的任何事他都觉得很棒，并且鼓励我做得更多。

sentences.en: When did you realize that perhaps that inner voice wasn't, was not there anymore, the harsh critic?
sentences.zh: 你是什么时候意识到那种内心的声音已经不在了，那个严厉的批评者不在了？

sentences.en: Because I think we do.
sentences.zh: 因为我觉得我们都有过。

sentences.en: Oh, it is.
sentences.zh: 哦，它还在。

sentences.en: It is?
sentences.zh: 还在？

sentences.en: Oh, it absolutely is.
sentences.zh: 哦，绝对还在。

sentences.en: But I think maybe when I was around 40, I started seeing a therapiSt.
sentences.zh: 但我想可能在我40岁左右时，我开始去看心理医生。

sentences.en: And what I learned from that is that when I hear that voice, I say, oh, that's my mother's voice.
sentences.zh: 我从中学到的是，当我听到那个声音时，我会说，哦，那是妈妈的声音。

sentences.en: That's not my voice.
sentences.zh: 那不是我的声音。

sentences.en: Because my mother always thought everything I would do would be a failure.
sentences.zh: 因为我妈妈总觉得我做的任何事情都会失败。

sentences.en: So, you know, her first reaction is, what makes you think that you can do that?
sentences.zh: 所以，你知道，她的第一反应是，你凭什么觉得你能做到？

sentences.en: And I just go, okay, that's my mother's voice.
sentences.zh: 而我只会想，好吧，那是妈妈的声音。

sentences.en: That's not my voice.
sentences.zh: 那不是我的声音。

sentences.en: And I just reinforce, okay, I'm going to try this.
sentences.zh: 我只是在心里强化，好吧，我要试试这个。

sentences.en: I don't know if I can do it, but I'm going to learn a lot from it.
sentences.zh: 我不知道自己能不能行，但我会从中学到很多。

sentences.en: And I'm always surprised how well it turns out.
sentences.zh: 而且结果往往让我感到惊喜。

sentences.en: And how do you deal with external pressure when people don't believe in you?
sentences.zh: 当人们不相信你时，你如何应对外部压力？

sentences.en: Because there's the internal voice and then there's, like, people in life who underestimate you.
sentences.zh: 因为除了内心的声音，生活中还有那些低估你的人。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah, there are a lot of them.
sentences.zh: 哦，对，这种人很多。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And I just have this philosophy, you're either on my train or just get off, get out of my way.
sentences.zh: 我一直有这样的人生哲学：你要么上我的车，要么就下车，别挡我的路。

sentences.en: I think because I had such a difficult time as a child, I don't like negative people around me.
sentences.zh: 我想是因为我童年过得很艰难，所以我周围不喜欢有负能量的人。

sentences.en: I just don't like to be with them.
sentences.zh: 我就是不喜欢跟他们在一起。

sentences.en: Um, so if you're going to be positive and you're going to bring things to the party, come along for the ride.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以如果你能保持积极，能为聚会带来快乐，那就一起上路吧。

sentences.en: But if you're going to be negative and question what I'm doing or not listen to what I want, um, just get out of my way.
sentences.zh: 但如果你总是很负能量，质疑我在做什么，或者不听取我的想法，嗯，那就别挡我的路。

sentences.en: Um.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Is that tough?
sentences.zh: 这样会不会太强硬？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不会。

sentences.en: You know what, I don't think it's tough, I think it's clear.
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，我不觉得这叫强硬，我觉得这叫界限清晰。

sentences.en: How then do you take feedback?
sentences.zh: 那你平时又是如何接受反馈的呢？

sentences.en: Oh, I ask for feedback all the time.
sentences.zh: 哦，我随时都会征求反馈。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: I mean, every morning I meet my team and we talk about what we're doing and I want to know what they think about it.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，每天早上我都会和团队开会，讨论我们在做的事情，我想知道他们的看法。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, it's my decision.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，决定权在我手里。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: And once I've made a decision, I don't want to discuss it.
sentences.zh: 一旦我做出了决定，我不想再讨论它。

sentences.en: I mean, now at this stage in your career, obviously people are going to be on the Ina train.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，现在到了你职业生涯的这个阶段，显然大家都愿意支持英娜。

sentences.en: Yes and no.
sentences.zh: 也不能全这么说。

sentences.en: Yes and no.
sentences.zh: 算是也不是吧。

sentences.en: But, I mean, you know, you are a person who has a proven track record.
sentences.zh: 不过，我的意思是，你知道的，你是一个有着公认成功业绩的人。

sentences.en: But when you were first trying to move into things.
sentences.zh: 但当你刚开始尝试涉足新领域的时候。

sentences.en: Well, I do remember my first book and my editor was the top cookbook editor in the country.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我确实记得我的第一本书，我的编辑是国内顶级的美食书编辑。

sentences.en: I mean, he was extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他非常了不起。

sentences.en: Really knowledgeable.
sentences.zh: 知识渊博。

sentences.en: I had some of the great, Martha Stewart, Lee Bailey, had really great authors.
sentences.zh: 我当时拥有一些很棒的作者，比如玛莎·斯图尔特、李·贝利。

sentences.en: And I have no idea why, but I would say to him, that's not the way I want to do it.
sentences.zh: 我也不知道为什么，但我会对他说，我不想那样做。

sentences.en: I want to do it this way.
sentences.zh: 我想这么做。

sentences.en: And he would disagree with me.
sentences.zh: 而他会反驳我。

sentences.en: He said, that's not the way it's done.
sentences.zh: 他说，不，不该这么做。

sentences.en: And I remember thinking, okay, well, I'm not going to be happy unless it's the way I want it done.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时想的是，好吧，如果不是按照我想要的方式去做，我是不会开心的。

sentences.en: And I don't know why I – I remember thinking how crazy it was to disagree with the top cookbook editor in the country.
sentences.zh: 我不知道为什么——我记得当时觉得自己居然敢反驳国内顶尖的美食书编辑，真是疯了。

sentences.en: But I just needed to have my vision in that book.
sentences.zh: 但我只是需要在书中体现我自己的愿景。

sentences.en: And I remember saying to myself, well, either I'm wrong and he'll never have to see me again or I'm right and he'll think I'm a genius.
sentences.zh: 我记得当时对自己说，要么是我错了，他以后再也不用见我了；要么是我对了，他会觉得我是个天才。

sentences.en: So I was just determined to make sure it was the way I wanted it to be.
sentences.zh: 所以我下定决心，一定要把它做成我想要的样子。

sentences.en: And that determination comes from the feeling that if you can't execute your vision, then it's not going to be satisfying.
sentences.zh: 这种决心来自于一种感觉：如果你无法实现自己的愿景，那么一切都不会让人满意。

sentences.en: And why bother doing it if you're just going to do what everybody else is doing?
sentences.zh: 如果你只是在重复别人的做法，那又何必去做呢？

sentences.en: But you have to have an idea.
sentences.zh: 但你必须得有想法。

sentences.en: You have to show up 100% and come with an idea.
sentences.zh: 你必须百分之百地投入，带着想法出现。

sentences.en: Martha Stewart helped launch you.
sentences.zh: 玛莎·斯图尔特曾助你一臂之力。

sentences.en: She did.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And in that early stage of your career, there was a lot of pressure to be a mini Martha.
sentences.zh: 在你职业生涯的早期，要成为“小玛莎”的压力很大。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: She had sort of created the mold and they wanted to have more –
sentences.zh: 她可以说是开创了一种模式，而他们希望有更多——

sentences.en: Well, that was one of the models.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是当时的众多模式之一。

sentences.en: That was one of the models.
sentences.zh: 那是当时的模式之一。

sentences.en: And she changed how it happened.
sentences.zh: 而且她改变了行业的发展方式。

sentences.en: I mean, she did it brilliantly in her vision.
sentences.zh: 我是说，她凭借自己的愿景做得非常出色。

sentences.en: I mean, you walked away from your first foray into television because they wanted you to be a mini Martha.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你放弃了第一次涉足电视的机会，因为他们想让你做一个“小玛莎”。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: How did you just have a sense that it wasn't the right fit?
sentences.zh: 你是怎么察觉到那并不适合你的？

sentences.en: I just don't know.
sentences.zh: 我其实也不知道。

sentences.en: You're stubborn, clearly.
sentences.zh: 显然你很固执。

sentences.en: I'm clear.
sentences.zh: 我这叫立场清晰。

sentences.en: I don't think stubborn is a bad word, by the way.
sentences.zh: 顺便说一句，我不认为“固执”是个贬义词。

sentences.en: I'm determined.
sentences.zh: 我只是有决心。

sentences.en: I think – well, it was her film crew that was filming a show for me.
sentences.zh: 我觉得——嗯，当时是她的摄制组在为我拍节目。

sentences.en: And they kept saying to me, no, no, no, you can't do it that way.
sentences.zh: 他们不停地对我说，不，不，不，你不能那样做。

sentences.en: And I was like – I kept saying to them, you have Martha.
sentences.zh: 而我——我一直在对他们说，你们已经有玛莎了。

sentences.en: You don't need me to be Martha.
sentences.zh: 你们不需要我来扮演玛莎。

sentences.en: You need me to be me.
sentences.zh: 你们需要我做我自己。

sentences.en: And I don't know why I knew that.
sentences.zh: 我不知道自己当时为什么会懂这个。

sentences.en: But I just was very clear that, you know, Martha does a certain – does things a certain way.
sentences.zh: 但我非常清楚，你知道的，玛莎有她的一套——做事有她的一套方式。

sentences.en: And I do them differently.
sentences.zh: 而我做的方式不同。

sentences.en: And unless that film reflected who I was, it was going to look like I was trying to be Martha.
sentences.zh: 除非那个镜头能反映出我是谁，否则看起来就像我在刻意模仿玛莎。

sentences.en: And that's not who I am.
sentences.zh: 而那不是真正的我。

sentences.en: According to a New Yorker profile of you from a few years ago, you and Martha grew apart.
sentences.zh: 根据几年前《纽约客》对你的一篇人物专访，你和玛莎的关系疏远了。

sentences.en: Can I just say I admire her enormously.
sentences.zh: 我能说我极其崇拜她吗？

sentences.en: I think what she created is stunning.
sentences.zh: 我认为她所创造的一切令人惊叹。

sentences.en: Are you friends?
sentences.zh: 你们现在是朋友吗？

sentences.en: And she did it with vision.
sentences.zh: 而且她是用宏大的愿景做到了这一点。

sentences.en: I mean, we're friendly.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们算是朋友。

sentences.en: We're not – there's no antipathy.
sentences.zh: 我们并没有——彼此之间没有任何敌意。

sentences.en: She moved to Bedford, and she used to live in East Hampton, so we saw each other then.
sentences.zh: 她搬到了贝德福德，以前她住在东汉普顿，所以那时候我们经常见面。

sentences.en: I mean, I know you get asked about Martha a lot.
sentences.zh: 我知道人们经常问你关于玛莎的事。

sentences.en: And in many ways, you became your own thing, the anti-Martha in some ways, you know, a different style of cooking.
sentences.zh: 在很多方面，你走出了自己的路，在某种程度上成了“反玛莎”，你知道的，有着不同的烹饪风格。

sentences.en: Is that in itself frustrating that you always get kind of put in some kind of juxtaposition of her?
sentences.zh: 你总是被拿来和她作比较，这本身会让你觉得沮丧吗？

sentences.en: I had an interesting conversation with Alison Roman recently, actually.
sentences.zh: 其实我最近和艾莉森·罗曼有过一次很有意思的交谈。

sentences.en: I said to her, you know, she and I are kind of in a continuum that started with Julia Child, who wanted to teach people how to cook with real food.
sentences.zh: 我对她说，你看，她和我其实都处在一个由朱莉娅·柴尔德开启的历史脉络中，朱莉娅当时想教人们如何用真正的食材做饭。

sentences.en: You know, when everybody was making, like, box macaroni and cheese, she wanted you to appreciate a really good beef bourguignon.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，当所有人都在吃那种盒装的通心粉配奶酪时，她却想让你去欣赏一份真正美味的勃艮第牛肉。

sentences.en: And then Martha came along and elevated home arts to something really worth doing well, set a beautiful table, make a wonderful dinner, carve out a pumpkin for the pumpkin soup.
sentences.zh: 然后玛莎出现了，她把家政艺术提升为了一件真正值得好好去做的事情：摆一张漂亮的桌子，做一顿美妙的晚餐，把南瓜挖空用来装南瓜汤。

sentences.en: It's just fabulous.
sentences.zh: 这简直太棒了。

sentences.en: I came along and said, okay, maybe not carve out the pumpkin, set a nice table.
sentences.zh: 而我的出现则是说，好吧，也许不用把南瓜挖空，但可以把桌子摆得好看点。

sentences.en: It doesn't have to be over the top, and make a lovely dinner and serve it.
sentences.zh: 没必要搞得过于隆重，做一顿可口的晚餐端上桌就行。

sentences.en: And then Alison Roman came along and said, forget setting the table.
sentences.zh: 接着艾莉森·罗曼又出现了，她说，别管什么摆桌子了。

sentences.en: Just put the pot of soup on the table and have a good time.
sentences.zh: 直接把一锅汤端上桌，大家吃得开心就好。

sentences.en: And so I think everybody's getting a little simpler and simpler, but at the end of the day, we all like the same thing, which is gathering people around a table.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为大家的风格越来越简单化，但归根结底，我们都喜欢同一件事，那就是把大家聚在餐桌旁。

sentences.en: You know, Alison Roman also said in that New Yorker profile that people were always asking her if she's a Martha or an Ina.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，艾莉森·罗曼在那篇《纽约客》专访中也提到，人们总是在问她究竟是“玛莎派”还是“英娜派”。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Oh, I don't remember that.
sentences.zh: 哦，我不记得这个了。

sentences.en: So there is, like, a sense of a continuum, but also a sort of dichotomy, if you will.
sentences.zh: 所以这既有一种传承感，但如果你愿意的话，也存在某种二元对立。

sentences.en: Yeah, I think we've each taken what's in the world and made it our own.
sentences.zh: 对，我认为我们都吸收了世上原有的东西，并将其转化成了我们自己的风格。

sentences.en: And the reason I ask also is because in that New Yorker profile, Martha said she had never made one of your recipes, which I felt was kind of pointed.
sentences.zh: 我问这个的原因还在于，在那篇《纽约客》专访中，玛莎说她从来没做过你的任何食谱，我觉得这话有点针对性。

sentences.en: I wonder if it bothered you.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这有没有困扰到你。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: It's certainly hers to decide.
sentences.zh: 这当然是她自己的决定。

sentences.en: It's – I didn't know what to make of that.
sentences.zh: 这——我不知道该怎么看待这件事。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: I've certainly made lots of hers.
sentences.zh: 我倒是做过很多她的食谱。

sentences.en: We've talked about how you've sort of evolved over time.
sentences.zh: 我们之前聊过你是如何一路发展过来的。

sentences.en: And I do want to touch on a period of your life that I find fascinating, which is your period at the Food Network.
sentences.zh: 我确实想聊聊你人生中一个我觉得非常迷人的时期，也就是你在美食频道的日子。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.zh: 哦。

sentences.en: Because it's really changed since you started there 20 years ago.
sentences.zh: 因为自从你20年前加入以来，那里真的发生了很大变化。

sentences.en: You know, you came up with Rachel Ray.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你是和雷切尔·雷同时代出来的。

sentences.en: You came up with Paula Deen.
sentences.zh: 你和保拉·迪恩也是同期。

sentences.en: And you women were really a big deal at that certain period of time.
sentences.zh: 在那个特定的时期，你们这些女性确实很有影响力。

sentences.en: There's a lot of competition shows now, though.
sentences.zh: 不过现在有很多竞技类的节目了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That doesn't interest me.
sentences.zh: 我对那个不感兴趣。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: A lot of sort of male energy, Guy Fieri, Pitmasters, Bobby Flay.
sentences.zh: 有很多偏向男性荷尔蒙的风格，比如盖伊·菲里、烤肉大师、鲍比·弗雷。

sentences.en: I watch a lot of Bobby Flay.
sentences.zh: 我经常看鲍比·弗雷的节目。

sentences.en: Can I just say how much I adore Bobby Flay?
sentences.zh: 我能说我有多崇拜鲍比·弗雷吗？

sentences.en: You can say.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: He's just extraordinary.
sentences.zh: 他实在太优秀了。

sentences.en: Would you ever compete with Bobby Flay?
sentences.zh: 你有没有想过和鲍比·弗雷同台竞技？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 绝不。

sentences.en: See, you know, I'm not a chef.
sentences.zh: 你看，我不是厨师。

sentences.en: I'm a home cook.
sentences.zh: 我只是个家庭厨子。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And, I mean, to go to Bobby's house and watch him just make lunch was not a recipe anywhere.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，去鲍比家里看他随手做个午餐，那根本不是按什么食谱来的。

sentences.en: I mean, he's, you know, he's run restaurants.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他经营过餐厅。

sentences.en: It's in his DNA.
sentences.zh: 烹饪已经融入了他的基因。

sentences.en: He's such an extraordinary cook.
sentences.zh: 他是一个如此卓越的厨师。

sentences.en: And he's so joyful in the kitchen.
sentences.zh: 而且他在厨房里总是充满快乐。

sentences.en: It's just wonderful to watch.
sentences.zh: 看他做饭简直是一种享受。

sentences.en: And, you know, he doesn't, when he's competing with somebody, this is their identifying recipe.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道的，当他和别人比赛时，那往往是对方的招牌食谱。

sentences.en: This is their favorite recipe.
sentences.zh: 那是他们最喜欢的食谱。

sentences.en: And Bobby's never seen it before.
sentences.zh: 而鲍比在此之前甚至都没见过。

sentences.en: And he usually beats them.
sentences.zh: 但他通常都能赢。

sentences.en: Why have you never wanted to be part of a competition show?
sentences.zh: 为什么你从来不想参加竞技类节目？

sentences.en: It's just not who I am.
sentences.zh: 那不是我的风格。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 而且你知道吗？

sentences.en: That's what other people do.
sentences.zh: 那是别人做的事。

sentences.en: I just like to do something different.
sentences.zh: 我只喜欢做点不一样的。

sentences.en: I think part of Food Network's DNA is showing people how to cook.
sentences.zh: 我认为美食频道的核心基因之一就是教人们如何做饭。

sentences.en: And, fortunately, they still support my doing it.
sentences.zh: 幸运的是，他们依然支持我这样做。

sentences.en: Warner Brothers, which runs the Food Network.
sentences.zh: 华纳兄弟公司目前运营着美食频道。

sentences.en: Is in the midst of possibly being sold to Paramount.
sentences.zh: 正处于可能被派拉蒙收购的过程中。

sentences.en: Not yet.
sentences.zh: 还没有。

sentences.en: Not so faSt.
sentences.zh: 没那么快。

sentences.en: Not so faSt.
sentences.zh: 没那么快。

sentences.en: I mean, do you have an opinion about that merger?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你对这桩并购有什么看法吗？

sentences.en: Will you stay with the Food Network if it gets sold?
sentences.zh: 如果美食频道被收购，你还会留下来吗？

sentences.en: I think I'm going to stay away from that one.
sentences.zh: 我想我还是别掺和这个了。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Is that all right?
sentences.zh: 这样可以吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 行。

sentences.en: I understand.
sentences.zh: 我理解。

sentences.en: It's complicated.
sentences.zh: 情况很复杂。

sentences.en: It's complicated.
sentences.zh: 情况很复杂。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Who would you say your audience is today?
sentences.zh: 你觉得你们现在的受众都是些什么人？

sentences.en: I'm sure you've thought about this as you're launching your new podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 我相信你在筹备新播客时一定思考过这个问题。

sentences.en: I mean, who do you think of as people who watch Ina Garten?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你认为谁会看伊娜·加滕的节目？

sentences.en: You know, it's astonishing to me how varied it is.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，受众群体如此多样化，这让我感到十分惊讶。

sentences.en: I just – I mean, I always – I've said this before that I loved walking up Madison Avenue one day and a woman in a big fur coat was like, oh, darling, love your cookbooks.
sentences.zh: 我只是——我是说，我一直——我以前就说过，我有一天很喜欢走在麦迪逊大道上，一个穿着大皮草大衣的女人跑来说，哦，亲爱的，太喜欢你的食谱了。

sentences.en: And a block later, a truck driver pulled over and said, hey, babe, love your show.
sentences.zh: 而在一个街区外，一个卡车司机把车停在路边说，嘿，宝贝，太喜欢你的节目了。

sentences.en: And I thought, this is what food is.
sentences.zh: 然后我想，这就是食物的意义。

sentences.en: And, I mean, I would think that my audience would be older because I am.
sentences.zh: 而且，我的意思是，我本来以为我的受众会偏向老年人，因为我也老了。

sentences.en: But, I mean, Gen Zers are just desperate to cook and entertain now and be together with their friends.
sentences.zh: 但是，我是说，现在的Z世代极其渴望做饭、招待客人，以及和朋友们聚在一起。

sentences.en: Have you seen the many social media accounts parodying you with love?
sentences.zh: 你见过网上那些充满爱意地恶搞你的社交账号吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Oh, really?
sentences.zh: 哦，真的吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: I would love to show you.
sentences.zh: 我很想给你看一看。

sentences.en: Like, in particular, you heard of a comedian called Tom Hearn?
sentences.zh: 比如，尤其是，你听说过一个叫汤姆·赫恩的喜剧演员吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 听过。

sentences.en: He does the shirt, the giant margarita glass.
sentences.zh: 他会穿那种衬衫，拿着巨大的玛格丽特酒杯。

sentences.en: But there's also just many, many others, you know.
sentences.zh: 但除此之外还有很多很多其他人，你知道的。

sentences.en: Somebody came to Jeffrey and said that they were having a wedding at Anne McGancet, which is the next town over from East Hampton,
sentences.zh: 有人对杰弗里说，他们在东汉普顿隔壁的安麦甘切特举办了一场婚礼，

sentences.en: and that all the bridesmaids were dressed like me.
sentences.zh: 而且所有的伴娘都打扮得像我一样。

sentences.en: And could I stop by?
sentences.zh: 问我能不能去露个面？

sentences.en: And I was like, are you kidding?
sentences.zh: 当时我就想，你开什么玩笑？

sentences.en: I mean, what were they going to explain to their kids in 10 years?
sentences.zh: 我是说，十年后他们要怎么跟自己的孩子解释？

sentences.en: Why everybody was dressed in a denim shirt?
sentences.zh: 为什么所有人当时都穿着牛仔衬衫？

sentences.en: I mean, it was incredibly flattering, but a little crazy.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这真的让人受宠若惊，但也稍微有点疯狂。

sentences.en: I mean, speaking of social media, what do you make of the influencers sort of online making, sort of elevating the old-fashioned idea of homemaking, you know, the trad wife trend,
sentences.zh: 说到社交媒体，你怎么看待网上那些网红把持家这种老派理念进行拔高，也就是所谓的“传统妻子”潮流，

sentences.en: wives who are farming their own food, making everything from scratch?
sentences.zh: 那些自己种地、所有东西都从头做起的妻子们？

sentences.en: It seems very different than what you've been advocating your whole career.
sentences.zh: 这似乎和你整个职业生涯一直倡导的理念大相径庭。

sentences.en: The only thing I advocate is do exactly what feels right to you, period.
sentences.zh: 我唯一倡导的就是：做那些让你觉得真正对的事，就这么简单。

sentences.en: Just don't become somebody else because you think it'll allow you to fit in.
sentences.zh: 千万不要为了合群而变成另一个人。

sentences.en: Figure out who you are and do what you want to do.
sentences.zh: 弄清楚你自己是谁，然后去做你想做的事。

sentences.en: If you want to stay home and cook and take care of the family, I think it's wonderful.
sentences.zh: 如果你想待在家里做饭、照顾家庭，我觉得这棒极了。

sentences.en: If you want to work, I think it's great.
sentences.zh: 如果你想工作，我也觉得很棒。

sentences.en: We're so busy judging everybody, and it's free.
sentences.zh: 我们总是忙着评判所有人，而且这又不需要成本。

sentences.en: You're just from the sidelines.
sentences.zh: 你只是站在场外。

sentences.en: You can just take pot shots at anybody.
sentences.zh: 随随便便就能对任何人冷嘲热讽。

sentences.en: And what's the point?
sentences.zh: 这又有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: Does it make you feel better?
sentences.zh: 这样能让你感觉好受点吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 并不能。

sentences.en: The reason I asked about sort of the trend of elevating the home arts and cooking your own food and all of that is because it did make me wonder if you ever had internal battles over your career with traditionally women-coded things because I see you as clearly a feminiSt.
sentences.zh: 我之所以问起这种推崇家庭艺术、自己做饭等潮流，是因为我很好奇，你是否曾在自己的职业生涯中经历过内心挣扎，纠结于那些传统上被贴上女性标签的事物，因为在我看来，你显然是一位女权主义者。

sentences.en: Is that how you would describe yourself, first of all?
sentences.zh: 首先，你会这样形容自己吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 会。

sentences.en: And how did you think about how you were sort of showing up with what you were doing?
sentences.zh: 那你当时是如何看待自己所作所为的呈现方式的呢？

sentences.en: Well, I'll tell you a story I've actually never told.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我跟你讲一个我从来没公开说过的事。

sentences.en: It's when I was in high school, the girls took home ec, and the boys took shop.
sentences.zh: 我读高中时，女生上家政课，男生上工场课。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And I don't think anybody had ever questioned that.
sentences.zh: 我觉得当时所有人对此都习以为常，从没产生过疑问。

sentences.en: And I just refused to take home ec.
sentences.zh: 而我就是拒绝上家政课。

sentences.en: And I took shop.
sentences.zh: 我去上了工场课。

sentences.en: And what I learned is drafting.
sentences.zh: 我学到的东西是制图。

sentences.en: And at some point I was thinking maybe I'd be an architect.
sentences.zh: 而且我有一段时间甚至考虑过以后当个建筑师。

sentences.en: But I use those drafting skills all the time.
sentences.zh: 但我现在一直在运用那些制图技能。

sentences.en: So now when I think back how ironic it is that I refused to do cooking and, you know, whatever Hulmec was at the time, I love what I do.
sentences.zh: 所以如今回想起来，我当年拒绝做饭以及当时所谓的家政课，是多么具有讽刺意味啊，但我真的很爱我现在做的事。

sentences.en: And I could actually make a case that I'm really lucky that I'm interested in a field where women excel so that the only limitation on my success was my own imagination.
sentences.zh: 其实我完全可以这么说：我很幸运，自己感兴趣的领域正是女性大放异彩的行业，因此我成功的唯一限制只有我自己的想象力。

sentences.en: And I think women in cookbooks and women in TV, I mean, it's easier.
sentences.zh: 我觉得女性在食谱界和电视界发展，我是说，相对容易一些。

sentences.en: So it was just a happy confluence.
sentences.zh: 所以这只是一次幸福的巧合。

sentences.en: I didn't choose it because it was a female talent.
sentences.zh: 我选择它不是因为这是女性的专长。

sentences.en: I just choose it because I love doing it.
sentences.zh: 我选择它纯粹是因为我热爱这份工作。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We are going to speak again, but this has been utterly delightful.
sentences.zh: 我们以后还会再聊，但这次的访谈真的非常愉快。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I appreciated your time.
sentences.zh: 感谢你抽出时间。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It was so much fun to be here with you.
sentences.zh: 今天能和你一起录节目真的太开心了。

sentences.en: On the interview, we talked to our guest twice.
sentences.zh: 在这次采访中，我们和嘉宾聊了两次。

sentences.en: So later, I followed up with Garten, who was at her home in East Hampton.
sentences.zh: 因此后来，我再次采访了加滕，当时她在东汉普顿的家中。

sentences.en: We got into her favorite ingredients and whether she's ever considered retiring.
sentences.zh: 我们聊了她最喜欢的食材，以及她是否曾考虑过退休。

sentences.en: I'm Wena Liu.
sentences.zh: 我是刘文娜。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times games.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》游戏板块字谜之一“连线”的作者。

sentences.en: And I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢我的狗。

sentences.en: And I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我也喜欢试图套路你们。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天负责制作“拼写蜜蜂”和“字母连线”游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called promesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的奇妙特质。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由真人制作的，就像你刚才听到声音的这些人一样。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 访问 nytimes.com 细斜杠 games 开始今天的游戏。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Ina, thank you so much for joining me again.
sentences.zh: 伊娜，非常感谢你再次接受我的采访。

sentences.en: It's nice to see you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Nice to see you again, too.
sentences.zh: 也很高兴再次见到你。

sentences.en: We had such a good time last time.
sentences.zh: 我们上次聊得非常开心。

sentences.en: You know, I was thinking, we had spoken earlier about how you ask yourself one question when deciding whether or not to do something right, and you said, is it going to be fun?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我在想，我们之前聊过你在决定是否要做某件事时会问自己一个问题，对吧，你说过，这会有趣吗？

sentences.en: But I was wondering about something for you that might have been really, really hard but not fun, that you're glad that you did in the end.
sentences.zh: 但我很好奇，有没有一件事对你来说非常非常难，但并不有趣，不过你最终还是很高兴自己做了这件事？

sentences.en: Do you have a story about that?
sentences.zh: 你有什么关于这方面的故事吗？

sentences.en: Something that was hard but not fun.
sentences.zh: 一件很难但并不有趣的事。

sentences.en: The thing about hard is I like having problems to solve.
sentences.zh: 关于困难，我的看法是，我喜欢有需要解决的问题。

sentences.en: So, if I have something that's difficult and I have to work it out, I find myself totally engaged in it, and I enjoy that process.
sentences.zh: 所以，如果遇到棘手的事情必须去解决，我会完全沉浸其中，并且我很享受这个过程。

sentences.en: So, I think that's fun, figuring it out.
sentences.zh: 因此，我觉得把问题琢磨透本身就很有趣。

sentences.en: Like, starting out going, how is this ever going to happen?
sentences.zh: 比如刚开始时会想，这到底要怎么实现啊？

sentences.en: And then you go, well, if I start it this way, and I go there, and then I try that, let me see where I am when I get there.
sentences.zh: 然后你会说，好吧，如果我从这里开始，然后去到那里，接着尝试那个，让我看看走到那一步时我在哪儿。

sentences.en: So, I like that.
sentences.zh: 所以，我喜欢这样。

sentences.en: I find that process fun.
sentences.zh: 我发现这个过程很有趣。

sentences.en: I mean, fun isn't always ha-ha fun.
sentences.zh: 我是说，“有趣”并不总是那种哈哈大笑的乐子。

sentences.en: Fun is just something that really feels good.
sentences.zh: 有趣只是指某件真正让人感觉很好的事情。

sentences.en: Are you a perfectionist?
sentences.zh: 你是个完美主义者吗？

sentences.en: I mean, you don't seem to be- I think the people around me might say I am.
sentences.zh: 我是说，你看上去不像——我想我身边的人可能会说我是。

sentences.en: I am in some ways.
sentences.zh: 我在某些方面确实是。

sentences.en: Yeah, I am.
sentences.zh: 是的，我是。

sentences.en: I like things done the way I want them done.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢按自己想要的方式把事情做好。

sentences.en: And do you think that's part of your success?
sentences.zh: 你觉得这也是你成功的原因之一吗？

sentences.en: That idea of it has to be on the Ina train or not on the Ina train?
sentences.zh: 那种必须按伊娜的规矩来或者别插手的理念？

sentences.en: I think that clarity is part of anybody's success, and I think I'm really clear about what is my brand and what I want to do to further that, rather than, you know, people
sentences.zh: 我认为这种清晰的自我认知是任何人成功的一部分，而且我觉得我非常清楚自己的品牌是什么，以及我想做什么来推动它发展，而不是像有些人那样，

sentences.en: having lots of ideas and going, well, let's try this and let's try that.
sentences.zh: 有一堆想法，然后说，好吧，我们试试这个，再试试那个。

sentences.en: I don't- you know, I've been doing this for 50 years, and I know what I like, and I think that's why people understand what I'm doing, because it's consistent.
sentences.zh: 我没有——你知道的，我做这行已经50年了，我很清楚自己喜欢什么，我想这也是为什么大家能理解我在做什么，因为我的风格始终如一。

sentences.en: I was thinking also about your origin story, because as we mentioned in our first conversation, you had a lot of trauma with your parents who didn't support you.
sentences.zh: 我还想到了你的身世背景，正如我们在第一次谈话中所提到的，你的父母并没有给予你支持，你在他们身上遭受了许多创伤。

sentences.en: They didn't believe in you.
sentences.zh: 他们不信任你。

sentences.en: What are some of those memories for you growing up in your house that sort of made you have this reaction of wanting to do something completely different?
sentences.zh: 在你的成长过程中，家里有哪些记忆让你产生了想要做一件完全不同的事情的叛逆想法？

sentences.en: I think I never had any agency whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我以前完全没有任何自主权。

sentences.en: Nobody ever asked, what would you like to do today?
sentences.zh: 从来没有人问过，你今天想做什么呀？

sentences.en: Or if I decided to do something, that was well done.
sentences.zh: 或者就算我决定做成一件事，也没有得到过肯定。

sentences.en: So I've taught myself how to do it myself.
sentences.zh: 所以我都是自学成才，自己摸索着怎么做。

sentences.en: I'm thinking of your mother's relationship to food.
sentences.zh: 我联想到了你母亲对食物的态度。

sentences.en: She was a nutritionist, right, who saw food as sort of a method of control and not of joy.
sentences.zh: 她是个营养学家，对吧？她把食物视为一种控制的手段，而不是快乐的源泉。

sentences.en: There was no joy in it.
sentences.zh: 食物里没有任何快乐可言。

sentences.en: I don't think she really understood joy.
sentences.zh: 我觉得她根本不懂什么是快乐。

sentences.en: I think if you go through a difficult time, you either allow it to affect you, or you decide you're going to do it differently.
sentences.zh: 我想，如果你经历了艰难的时期，要么你任由它影响你，要么你决定换一种活法。

sentences.en: And I absolutely deliberately decided to do it differently.
sentences.zh: 而我绝对是刻意决定要活得不一样。

sentences.en: And I just love having a good time.
sentences.zh: 我就是喜欢过得开开心心的。

sentences.en: And I don't see any reason why I shouldn't.
sentences.zh: 而且我觉得没有任何理由不这么做。

sentences.en: So I always go towards that.
sentences.zh: 所以我总是朝着那个方向努力。

sentences.en: I go towards people that are happy.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢跟快乐的人交往。

sentences.en: I go towards people, projects that will be fun to do or be satisfying.
sentences.zh: 我倾向于选择那些做起来有趣或能带来满足感的人和项目。

sentences.en: As you say, fun isn't always like, you know, going down a water slide.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，有趣并不总是像去玩水上滑梯那样。

sentences.en: Fun is building something with people that you care about.
sentences.zh: 有趣是和你在乎的人一起创造某些成果。

sentences.en: You and Jeffrey decided pretty early on not to have kids, and you've talked about that.
sentences.zh: 你和杰弗里很早就决定不要孩子，你也谈过这个话题。

sentences.en: When you look at your peers who've raised kids, do you think you could have had the career that you've had if you had been a mom?
sentences.zh: 当你看着那些抚养了孩子的同龄人时，你觉得如果你当了妈妈，还能拥有现在的职业生涯吗？

sentences.en: I think it would have been difficult, and I think Jeffrey and I would have had a different life together, and we would have had a good life.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这会很艰难，而且我和杰弗里的人生轨迹也会不一样，不过我们本来也能过上好日子。

sentences.en: It doesn't—I'm not saying it's a better life or a worse life, but there were times when Jeffrey was—decided that he wanted to start a business in Japan.
sentences.zh: 这并不是说——我不是在比较怎样的人生更好或更糟，只是有时候，杰弗里决定在日本创业。

sentences.en: And so he moved to Japan.
sentences.zh: 于是他搬去了日本。

sentences.en: I was in East Hampton.
sentences.zh: 而我留在了东汉普顿。

sentences.en: We went back and forth, and we figured it out.
sentences.zh: 我们两头跑，最后把问题解决了。

sentences.en: So I think that that probably couldn't have happened, and I couldn't have stayed long hours at the store doing catering and running the specialty food store.
sentences.zh: 所以我想，如果有了孩子，这一切可能就不会发生，我也无法在店里长时间工作来负责餐饮外送并经营那家特色食品店了。

sentences.en: I think it would have been much harder, and I've never looked back on the decision and thought I should have done it differently.
sentences.zh: 我想那样会难得多，而且我从未回过头去看那个决定，并认为我当初应该采取不同的做法。

sentences.en: I mean, I understand how my friends have wonderful families, and they really enjoy being parents,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我理解我的朋友们有着美满的家庭，他们真的很享受当父母的过程，

sentences.en: but it's just not something I ever wanted to do, and I'm really happy that I didn't.
sentences.zh: 但这从来就不是我想做的事，而且我真的很高兴我没有那样做。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I'm going to do a final lightning round, if that's okay.
sentences.zh: 如果可以的话，接下来我要进行最后一轮快问快答。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Favorite person you've ever cooked for?
sentences.zh: 你为之做过饭的人当中，最喜欢谁？

sentences.en: Cooked for?
sentences.zh: 为谁做过饭？

sentences.en: Well, I actually had Eric Repair come for lunch recently, and I love to cook for him because he's not only an incredible chef, but he's also an appreciative gueSt.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我其实不久前刚请埃里克·雷佩尔来吃过午饭，我特别喜欢为他做饭，因为他不仅是一位出色的厨师，而且也是一个懂得欣赏的食客。

sentences.en: And when someone like that comes, are you trying to up your game?
sentences.zh: 当这样的人来作客时，你会不会想要拿出更高的水平？

sentences.en: Do you ask them what they'd like, or how are you preparing?
sentences.zh: 你会问他们想吃什么，还是会怎么准备？

sentences.en: I know what he likes, and I love to prepare it, so it's just really fun.
sentences.zh: 我知道他喜欢什么，我也很喜欢做这些，所以真的很有趣。

sentences.en: What did you make?
sentences.zh: 你做了什么？

sentences.en: I made a filet of beef with basil parmesan mayonnaise and a Charlie bird salad, and I served a red sancerre, which was slightly chilled and was just delicious.
sentences.zh: 我做了罗勒帕马森蛋黄酱烤牛里脊配查理伯德沙拉，还端上了一款稍微冰镇过的红桑塞尔葡萄酒，味道好极了。

sentences.en: Sounds wonderful, making me hungry.
sentences.zh: 听起来太棒了，我都听饿了。

sentences.en: Best advice you've ever gotten for how to live a good life?
sentences.zh: 你收到的关于如何过好一生的最好建议是什么？

sentences.en: Do what you love.
sentences.zh: 做你热爱的事。

sentences.en: If you love it, you'll be really good at it.
sentences.zh: 如果你热爱它，你就会把它做得非常好。

sentences.en: And that was, I think, Jeffrey who told you that.
sentences.zh: 我想，那是杰弗里告诉你的吧。

sentences.en: That was indeed Jeffrey.
sentences.zh: 确实是杰弗里。

sentences.en: That was the beginning of my life.
sentences.zh: 那是我人生的开端。

sentences.en: Customer pet peeve.
sentences.zh: 顾客最让人头疼的地方。

sentences.en: Help me not be a bad customer.
sentences.zh: 帮帮我，让我别做一个糟糕的顾客。

sentences.en: I think, I actually said this, I think that everybody should work in retail, like military service, so they understand how difficult it is.
sentences.zh: 我想，我其实说过这个，我认为每个人都应该去零售业工作，就像服兵役一样，这样他们就能明白这有多难。

sentences.en: And I think they'll have more respect for waiters and for people who work in restaurants and retail stores.
sentences.zh: 我想这样他们就会对服务员以及在餐馆和零售店工作的人有更多尊重。

sentences.en: What do you want people to learn?
sentences.zh: 你想让人们学到什么？

sentences.en: A little kindness?
sentences.zh: 一点善意？

sentences.en: It's a hard job.
sentences.zh: 这是一份辛苦的工作。

sentences.en: A little kindness, yeah.
sentences.zh: 一点善意，是的。

sentences.en: That the people working there aren't just functionaries.
sentences.zh: 那就是在那里工作的人不仅仅是机械执行公务的人。

sentences.en: They're actually people.
sentences.zh: 他们其实也是活生生的人。

sentences.en: And a little kindness goes a long way.
sentences.zh: 而且一点点善意能产生很大的影响。

sentences.en: Three most important ingredients to always have at hand, and what is the most overrated ingredient?
sentences.zh: 手头必须随时备有的三种最重要的配料是什么？最被高估的配料又是什么？

sentences.en: Three most important ingredients.
sentences.zh: 三种最重要的配料。

sentences.en: I would say good olive oil, French butter with flaked sea salt, and I think lemons.
sentences.zh: 我会说是好的橄榄油、带片状海盐的法国黄油，还有柠檬。

sentences.en: I love lemon on lots of things because you can use the grated zest, you can use the juice, and it kind of brings out the flavors of a lot of things.
sentences.zh: 我很喜欢在很多东西上加柠檬，因为你可以用擦出的柠檬皮屑，也可以用柠檬汁，它能在某种程度上激发很多食物的风味。

sentences.en: And what's the most overrated?
sentences.zh: 那什么是最被高估的？

sentences.en: I might say like granulated garlic in a spice jar.
sentences.zh: 我可能会说是香料罐里的那种颗粒状大蒜粉。

sentences.en: Why not just use regular garlic?
sentences.zh: 为什么不直接用普通大蒜呢？

sentences.en: I'm glad you didn't say salt, but salt is indeed the most important ingredient.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴你没说盐，但盐确实是最重要的配料。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Finally, because at this stage you don't need to achieve anything more.
sentences.zh: 最后，因为在这个阶段你已经不需要再去达成什么成就了。

sentences.en: You're beloved, you're famous, you're successful.
sentences.zh: 你备受喜爱，你出了名，你很成功。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Have you flirted with the idea of calling it quits?
sentences.zh: 你有没有动过金盆洗手、不再干了的念头？

sentences.en: Never.
sentences.zh: 从来没有。

sentences.en: Never?
sentences.zh: 从来没有？

sentences.en: Never.
sentences.zh: 从来没有。

sentences.en: I can't even imagine doing that.
sentences.zh: 我甚至无法想象那样做。

sentences.en: People ask my wonderful agent, Esther Newberg, if she's ever going to retire.
sentences.zh: 人们问我出色的经纪人埃丝特·纽伯格，她是否打算退休。

sentences.en: And she says, now, they pay me to read books, why would I retire?
sentences.zh: 而她说，开玩笑吧，他们付钱让我看书，我为什么要退休？

sentences.en: And I kind of feel the same way.
sentences.zh: 我也有点这种感觉。

sentences.en: I love what I do.
sentences.zh: 我热爱我的工作。

sentences.en: I love getting up in the morning and having a challenge for the day.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢早上醒来，迎接当天的挑战。

sentences.en: I just, I have the life I've always wanted.
sentences.zh: 我只是，我过着我一直想要的生活。

sentences.en: So why stop?
sentences.zh: 那为什么要停下来呢？

sentences.en: Why stop?
